questions.question: What was India’s global rank in the aviation market according to the International Aviation Data 2024 report released in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **International Aviation Data 2024** report released in **2025**, **India** has secured the **5th rank** in the **global aviation market**.
 
• This ranking is a reflection of the total **passenger traffic**, which includes both **domestic** and **international** travelers handled by Indian airports throughout the **calendar year 2024**.
 
• The report highlights that **India** has shown one of the highest **year-on-year growth rates** in the aviation sector, significantly outpacing many developed economies in **Europe**.
 
• Key factors contributing to this **5th position** include the rapid expansion of **low-cost carriers (LCCs)** and the modernization of major **aviation hubs** like **Delhi** and **Mumbai**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 5th.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Domestic Market Standing**: While India is ranked **5th** in the overall global market, it consistently maintains its position as the **3rd largest domestic aviation market** in the world, following the **United States** and **China**.
 
• **UDAN Scheme**: The **Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik (UDAN)**, a **Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS)** launched in **October 2016**, has been instrumental in operationalizing **unserved** and **underserved** airports, bringing air travel to **Tier-2** and **Tier-3** cities.
 
• **Fleet Expansion**: Major Indian airlines such as **IndiGo** and **Air India** made global headlines by placing record-breaking orders for over **1,100 aircraft** in recent years, ensuring a steady supply of capacity for future demand.
 
• **Airport Infrastructure**: The number of **operational airports** in India has grown from **74** in **2014** to over **149** by the end of **2024**. The government aims to reach **220 airports** by **2025** through the **National Infrastructure Pipeline**.
 
• **Regulatory Authority**: The **Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)** is the statutory body of the **Government of India** that regulates civil aviation, focusing on safety issues and **airworthiness** standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Greenfield Airports**: The **Government of India** has accorded 'in-principle' approval for setting up **21 Greenfield Airports** across the country, with major projects like **Noida International Airport (Jewar)** and **Navi Mumbai International Airport** expected to boost capacity significantly.
 
• **Air Cargo Growth**: Beyond passenger travel, India is striving to become a global **cargo hub**. The **Krishi Udan** scheme is a specific initiative designed to assist **farmers** in transporting **perishable agricultural products** to both **domestic** and **international** markets.
 
• **MRO Hub**: India is actively developing as a **Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO)** destination to reduce the dependency on foreign facilities and save **foreign exchange**.
 
• **Digital Initiatives**: The **DigiYatra** initiative, utilizing **Facial Recognition Technology (FRT)**, has been rolled out across several airports to provide a **seamless** and **paperless** entry process for passengers.
</ul

questions.question: Lamine Yamal, who won the Breakthrough of the Year award in 2025, plays which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Football**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lamine Yamal** is a world-renowned professional **Football** player from **Spain** who plays as a **winger**.
 
• In **2025**, he was honored with the **Laureus World Breakthrough of the Year** award, recognizing his extraordinary rise in the sport of **football** over the preceding year.
 
• He currently plays for the Spanish giant **FC Barcelona** and represents the **Spain national team** at the international level.
 
• Yamal gained global prominence during the **UEFA Euro 2024**, where he played a central role in leading **Spain** to their **fourth European Championship** title.
 
• He was awarded the **Young Player of the Tournament** trophy at **Euro 2024**, having recorded **four assists** and **one goal** during the competition.
 
• By winning the **Laureus Breakthrough** award, he joined an elite list of athletes who achieved global stardom at a very young age, often being compared to legends like **Lionel Messi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early Career and La Masia**: **Lamine Yamal** was born on **July 13, 2007**, in **Esplugues de Llobregat**, **Spain**. He joined **La Masia**, the famous youth academy of **FC Barcelona**, at the age of seven, where he was quickly identified as one of the most promising talents in **football**.
 
• **FC Barcelona Debut**: He made his senior debut for **FC Barcelona** on **April 29, 2023**, against **Real Betis**. At **15 years, 9 months, and 16 days** old, he became the youngest player to ever play for the club's first team in **La Liga** history.
 
• **Kopa Trophy**: Prior to his 2025 Laureus success, Yamal won the **2024 Kopa Trophy** at the **Ballon d'Or** ceremony, an award given to the best performing **football** player in the world under the age of **21**.
 
• **International Impact**: He chose to represent **Spain** despite having heritage from **Equatorial Guinea** and **Morocco**. He became **Spain's youngest ever player and goalscorer** during a match against **Georgia** in **September 2023** at the age of **16 years and 57 days**.
 
• **Market Value and Influence**: By the age of **17**, his market valuation exceeded **150 million Euros**, making him one of the most valuable **football** players on the planet. His playing style is characterized by elite **dribbling**, **close control**, and a powerful **left-footed** shot from the right flank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Youngest Records**: **Lamine Yamal** holds the record for being the **youngest player** to ever feature in a **UEFA European Championship** final and the **youngest goalscorer** in the history of the tournament.
 
• **Laureus World Sports Awards**: These awards are held annually to honor the greatest sporting achievements. The **Breakthrough of the Year** category specifically targets athletes who have made a significant leap in their career rankings or status.
 
• **2024-2025 Season**: During this period, Yamal became a permanent fixture in the **Barcelona** starting eleven, contributing to numerous victories in **La Liga** and the **UEFA Champions League**.
 
• **Youth Recognition**: He is the first player in history to be nominated for the **Ballon d'Or** while still being a **minor** (under the age of 18).
</ul

questions.question: What was the main objective of the Esports Conclave 2025 held in India?

options.text: To promote esports as a serious career and sporting option
To promote board games in schools

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote esports as a serious career and sporting option**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Esports Conclave 2025** was organized as a landmark event in **India** to address the rapidly evolving landscape of **competitive digital gaming**.
 
• The primary objective of the conclave was to **promote esports** as a legitimate and **serious career path**, moving beyond the perception of gaming as a mere hobby. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 3.***
 
• It aimed to bridge the gap between **professional players**, **investors**, and **policymakers** to establish a robust **sporting ecosystem** within the country.
 
• The event focused on the **professionalization** of the sector, discussing **training modules**, **athlete management**, and the creation of **dedicated infrastructure** for tournaments.
 
• It emphasized the **socio-economic impact** of esports, highlighting how it can generate **employment opportunities** in sectors like **broadcasting**, **event management**, and **game development**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Esports vs. Online Gaming**:
 
 
• **Esports** refers to **skill-based competitive gaming** where individuals or teams compete under a regulated set of rules, similar to traditional sports.
 
• The conclave sought to differentiate this from **casual online gaming** or **gambling**, ensuring a clear **regulatory framework** for competitive integrity.
 
 
 
• **Market Growth in India**:
 
 
• India has become one of the **world's largest markets** for gaming due to the deep **penetration of smartphones** and affordable **mobile data**.
 
• The number of **professional esports players** in India has seen an exponential rise, with **international tournaments** now offering prize pools worth **millions of dollars**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context**:
 
 
• Esports has gained **international recognition**, being featured as a **medal sport** in the **Asian Games 2022** (held in 2023) and the upcoming **Olympic Esports Games**.
 
• Such global milestones have paved the way for **national governments** to include esports in their **national sports policies**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Recognition**: In **December 2022**, the **Government of India** officially recognized esports as a part of **"multi-sports events"** under the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• **Skill-Based Development**: The focus of the **2025 Conclave** was also on the **mental and physical well-being** of players, advocating for a holistic approach to **athlete training**.
 
• **Inclusivity**: The conclave discussed **gender inclusivity** in gaming, encouraging more **women participation** in the professional esports arena to diversify the **talent pool**.
 
• **Technological Integration**: Discussions included the role of **5G technology**, **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, and **Cloud Gaming** in enhancing the competitive experience for Indian athletes.
</ul

questions.question: On 6 November 2025, where was the Indian Navy’s survey ship INS Ikshak commissioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kochi**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Indian Navy** officially commissioned its second **Survey Vessel (Large)**, **INS Ikshak**, on **6 November 2025**. 
• The commissioning ceremony was held at the **Naval Base** in **Kochi**, attended by senior military officials and dignitaries from the **Ministry of Defence**. 
• **INS Ikshak** is the second of **four** such vessels being built under the **SVL Project** by **Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE)**, **Kolkata**, in collaboration with **L&T Shipbuilding**. 
• The vessel's name, '**Ikshak**', translates to '**Guide**', representing the ship's primary mission of ensuring safe passage for mariners through precise maritime mapping. 
• This ship is a testament to **India's** growing maritime strength and its commitment to the **Make in India** initiative, boasting over **80% indigenous content** by cost. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Survey Vessel Large (SVL) Project:** 
• The project was initiated to replace the existing **Sandhayak-class** survey ships with more advanced platforms. 
• The contract for **four** **SVL** ships was signed in **October 2018** between the **Ministry of Defence** and **GRSE**. 
• **INS Sandhayak**, the first ship of this class, was commissioned earlier in **February 2024** at **Visakhapatnam**. 
• **Technical Capabilities and Features:** 
• The ship has a length of **110 meters** and a displacement of approximately **3,400 tons**. 
• It is equipped with highly sophisticated **hydrographic** equipment, including **Multi-beam Echo Sounders** and **Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs)**. 
• The vessel is powered by **two diesel engines** and can maintain a cruising speed of **14 knots**, with a maximum speed of **18 knots**. 
• **Operational Roles:** 
• The primary role involves conducting full-scale coastal and deep-water **hydrographic surveys** of **ports**, **harbors**, and **Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ)**. 
• It is designed to collect **oceanographic** and **geophysical** data for both **military** and **civilian** applications. 
• In times of emergency, the ship can be repurposed for **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR)** and can function as a **hospital ship**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The induction of **INS Ikshak** into the **Southern Naval Command** will significantly enhance the **Indian Navy's** capability to map the seabed in the strategic **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**. 
• The ship's advanced sensors and **Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs)** allow for high-resolution underwater data collection, which is vital for **submarine operations** and **maritime security**. 
• The **SVL** ships carry **four Survey Motor Boats**, which act as force multipliers during shallow water survey operations. 
• The commissioning reinforces **India's** role as a **Net Security Provider** and a leader in **hydrography** in the **Indo-Pacific** region. </ul

questions.question: In 2025, India celebrated the 10th anniversary of which major urban development scheme?

options.text: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smart City Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Smart Cities Mission** (SCM) was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **June 25, 2015**. Since it completes a decade of implementation in **2025**, the nation celebrates its **10th anniversary**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Smart City Mission.***
 
• The mission was designed to promote **100 cities** that provide core infrastructure, a clean and sustainable environment, and a decent quality of life to their citizens through the application of **"Smart Solutions"**.
 
• It is a centrally sponsored scheme where the **Central Government** provides financial support to the tune of **Rs. 48,000 crore** over five years, with a matching contribution from the **State Governments** and **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)**.
 
• The implementation of the mission is done by a **Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)** at the city level. Each SPV is headed by a full-time **CEO** and has nominees from the Central Government, State Government, and the ULB on its Board.
 
• The strategic components of the **Smart Cities Mission** include **City Improvement (Retrofitting)**, **City Renewal (Redevelopment)**, and **City Extension (Greenfield Development)**, plus a **Pan-city initiative** in which Smart Solutions are applied covering larger parts of the city.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)**:
 
 
• Launched on **June 25, 2015**, alongside the Smart City Mission. While it also celebrates its **10th anniversary** in **2025**, the question specifically focuses on the urban development scheme often highlighted for its "Smart" technological interventions.
 
• It covers **500 cities** and focuses on establishing infrastructure that could ensure adequate robust **sewage networks** and **water supply** for urban transformation.
 
• In **October 2021**, **AMRUT 2.0** was launched to make cities **'water secure'** and provide functional tap connections to all households in all statutory towns.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U)**:
 
 
• Launched on **June 25, 2015**, with the objective of providing **"Housing for All"** by the year 2022 (later extended).
 
• It addresses urban housing shortage among the **EWS/LIG** and **MIG** categories, including slum dwellers, by ensuring a **pucca house** to all eligible urban households.
 
• The mission has four verticals: **In-situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR)**, **Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS)**, **Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP)**, and **Beneficiary-led Individual House Construction (BLC)**.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Urban)**:
 
 
• Launched on **October 2, 2014**, to accelerate the efforts to achieve universal sanitation coverage.
 
• By **2025**, it would be in its **11th year** of implementation, having transitioned into **SBM-U 2.0** in **2021**, focusing on **Garbage Free Cities**.
 
• It aims at **100% scientific management** of municipal solid waste and making all statutory towns **Open Defecation Free (ODF)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nodal Ministry**: All the schemes mentioned above (SCM, AMRUT, PMAY-U, and SBM-U) are governed by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**, Government of India.
 
• **Integrated Command and Control Centers (ICCC)**: One of the most significant achievements of the **Smart City Mission** is the operationalization of **ICCCs** in almost all 100 cities, which acted as war rooms during the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• **Data and Impact**: As of recent reports, over **8,000 projects** worth more than **Rs. 1.6 lakh crore** have been part of the SCM pipeline, significantly impacting **urban mobility**, **public safety**, and **environmental monitoring**.
</ul

questions.question: The Ministry of Minority Affairs launched the Skilling and Women Entrepreneurship Development project at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) Kottayam in July 2025 to train minority youth and women in which of the following fields?

options.text: Internet of Things (IoT) and leadership skills

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Internet of Things (IoT) and leadership skills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** initiated the **Skilling and Women Entrepreneurship Development** project in **July 2025**. This project serves as a strategic intervention to bridge the digital and skill gap among marginalized sections of society.
 
• The project is hosted and executed at the **Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) Kottayam**, an institution of national importance located in **Kerala**. The collaboration aims to utilize the technical infrastructure and academic excellence of the institute.
 
• The curriculum specifically focuses on **Internet of Things (IoT)** training, enabling participants to understand and build connected systems, which is a critical component of **Industry 4.0**.
 
• A unique feature of this project is the integration of **leadership skills** alongside technical modules. This dual approach ensures that **minority youth** and **women** are not just prepared for jobs but are also equipped to start their own ventures as **entrepreneurs**.
 
• The project targets the socio-economic empowerment of the **minority communities**, focusing on increasing their participation in the high-tech workforce and the **startup ecosystem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Minority Affairs:** 
 
 
• Established in **January 2006**, this ministry focuses on the development and empowerment of notified minority communities, including **Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis,** and **Jains**.
 
• It implements various schemes such as **Naya Savera**, **Nai Roshni**, and **Seekho aur Kamao** to enhance educational and professional opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Internet of Things (IoT):** 
 
 
• **IoT** refers to a network of physical objects embedded with sensors, software, and other technologies to connect and exchange **data** with other devices over the internet.
 
• Applications of **IoT** span across **smart homes**, **healthcare**, **agriculture**, and **industrial automation**, making it a high-demand skill in the **2025** global economy.
 
 
 
• **IIIT Kottayam:** 
 
 
• Located at **Valavoor** in **Kottayam**, **Kerala**, it is one of the **IIITs** established by the **Government of India** under the **Public-Private Partnership (PPP)** mode.
 
• The institute offers specialized courses in **Computer Science**, **Cyber Security**, and **Data Science**, providing an ideal environment for advanced technical skilling projects.
 
 
 
• **Entrepreneurship and Leadership:** 
 
 
• The inclusion of **leadership skills** is aligned with the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which emphasizes holistic development and vocational training.
 
• Developing **leadership skills** helps in decision-making, team management, and **strategic planning**, which are essential for the success of **women-led startups**.
 
 
 
• **Skill India Mission:** 
 
 
• This project contributes to the broader **Skill India Mission** launched in **2015**, aiming to create a workforce that can meet the challenges of the **global market** through continuous **upskilling** and **reskilling**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gender Inclusivity:** The project prioritizes **women** to improve the **Female Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** in the technology sector.
 
• **Geographic Impact:** While located in **Kottayam**, the model is designed to be scalable, potentially serving as a blueprint for other **IIITs** across **India**.
 
• **Technological Advancement:** By focusing on **IoT**, the government ensures that **minority youth** are trained in **future-ready technologies** rather than traditional, low-value skills.
</ul

questions.question: Who among the following is the head of the 7-member committee set up by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in February 2025 to examine and suggest amendments to the Insurance Act, 1938?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dinesh Khara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** constituted a high-level **7-member committee** to review and suggest comprehensive amendments to the **Insurance Act, 1938**.
 
• The committee is chaired by **Dinesh Khara**, who is the **former Chairman of the State Bank of India (SBI)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Dinesh Khara.***
 
• The primary objective of this panel is to modernize the legal framework governing the insurance sector to align with the government's vision of **"Insurance for All by 2047"**.
 
• The committee's mandate includes examining provisions related to **capital requirements**, **solvency margins**, and the potential introduction of **composite insurance licenses**, which would allow a single company to offer both life and general insurance products.
 
• This move is expected to enhance the **ease of doing business**, attract more investment, and increase **insurance penetration** across the country by removing outdated regulatory hurdles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**:
 
 
• It is the **statutory body** responsible for regulating and promoting the insurance and re-insurance industries in India.
 
• It was established in **1999** following the recommendations of the **Malhotra Committee** report.
 
• The headquarters of **IRDAI** is located in **Hyderabad**, Telangana, and its current **Chairman** is **Debasish Panda**.
 
 
 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938**:
 
 
• This is the fundamental law that provides the framework for the **regulation** of the insurance business in India.
 
• Major amendments were made in **2015** and **2021**; the latter notably increased the **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** limit in the insurance sector from **49% to 74%**.
 
 
 
• **Dinesh Khara**:
 
 
• He served as the **Chairman of the State Bank of India** from **October 2020** until **August 2024**.
 
• Under his leadership, **SBI** achieved significant milestones in **digital banking** and **profitability**, making his expertise vital for the structural reform of the insurance sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Analysis**:
 
 
• **Swaminathan Janakiraman**: He is currently a **Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and previously served as a Managing Director at **SBI**.
 
• **Ajay Tyagi**: He is a former **Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**, having served from **2017 to 2022**.
 
• **TS Vijayan**: He is a former **Chairman** of both the **Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)** and the **IRDAI**.
 
 
 
• **Composite Licensing**: This is a major reform being discussed by the **Dinesh Khara committee**. Currently, Indian law requires separate entities for life, general, and health insurance. questions.question: In August 2025, who assumed charge as the Director General of the Railway Protection Force (RPF), becoming the first woman to head the 143-year-old central security force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sonali Mishra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sonali Mishra**, an officer of the **1993 batch** of the **Indian Police Service (IPS)** from the **Madhya Pradesh cadre**, took charge as the **Director General (DG)** of the **Railway Protection Force (RPF)** in **August 2025**.
 
• She created history by becoming the **first woman** to head the **Railway Protection Force**, a security wing that has been in existence for **143 years**.
 
• Her appointment was formalized following the approval of the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)**, succeeding **Manoj Yadava**, who retired from the post on **July 31, 2025**.
 
• Before her elevation to this **top designation**, she served as the **Additional Director General (ADG)** of the **Border Security Force (BSF)**, where she commanded the **Eastern Command** headquartered in **Kolkata**.
 
• As the **Director General**, she is responsible for the overall administration of the force, ensuring the **security of railway property** and the safety of **millions of passengers** across the **Indian Railways** network.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Railway Protection Force (RPF):**
 
 
• The **RPF** is a **security force** under the ownership of the **Ministry of Railways**, **Government of India**.
 
• It was originally established in **1872** by various railway companies and was given statutory status under the **RPF Act, 1957**.
 
• In **1985**, it was declared an **Armed Force of the Union** through an amendment to the **RPF Act**.
 
• The force is unique as it has the **legal power** to search, arrest, and prosecute offenses under the **Railway Property (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1966**.
 
 
 
• **Nina Singh:**
 
 
• A **1989-batch IPS officer** of the **Rajasthan cadre**, she became the **first woman** to be appointed as the **Director General** of the **Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)** in **December 2023**.
 
 
 
• **Archana Ramasundram:**
 
 
• She is a **1980-batch IPS officer** who became the **first woman** to head a **Central Armed Police Force (CAPF)** when she was appointed as the **Director General** of the **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** in **2016**.
 
 
 
• **Rashmi Shukla:**
 
 
• A **1988-batch IPS officer**, she served as the **Director General** of the **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** and later became the **first woman Director General of Police (DGP)** of **Maharashtra** in **January 2024**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Women Empowerment in Security Forces:** The appointment of **Sonali Mishra** reflects the increasing representation of **women** in **leadership roles** within India’s **paramilitary** and **central security forces**.
 
• **Force Mandate:** The **RPF** currently consists of over **70,000 personnel**. They are primarily tasked with the **protection and security** of **Railway Property**, **passenger areas**, and the **well-being of passengers**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The transition of the **RPF** from a "Watch and Ward" staff in **1872** to a **federal armed force** marks its significant **evolution** in the **Indian administrative system**.
 
• **Administrative Control:** Unlike other **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)** which fall under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, the **RPF** functions directly under the **Ministry of Railways**.

questions.question: Which three economies topped the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switzerland, Singapore, and Hong Kong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IMD World Competitiveness Ranking**, released in **June 2025**, identifies the most competitive economies globally based on their ability to create and maintain an environment that sustains the competitiveness of enterprises.
 
• **Singapore** returned to a leading position in the **2025** rankings, showcasing exceptional strength in **Business Efficiency** and **Economic Performance**. Its robust digital infrastructure and openness to **International Trade** were pivotal factors.
 
• **Switzerland** maintained its elite status in the top three, primarily due to its world-class **Infrastructure**, high-quality **Education system**, and stable **Government Efficiency**. It continues to lead in categories related to **Scientific Infrastructure** and **Institutional Framework**.
 
• **Hong Kong** secured a spot in the top three economies, reflecting its resurgence as a global financial hub. The region demonstrated significant improvements in **International Investment** and **Tax Policy**, which bolstered its overall **Government Efficiency** score.
 
• The **2025** edition of the ranking evaluated a total of **67 global economies**, providing a comprehensive benchmark for policymakers and business leaders to assess national performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The IMD World Competitiveness Center:**
 
 
• It is a research group at the **International Institute for Management Development (IMD)** located in **Lausanne, Switzerland**. It has been publishing these rankings annually since **1989**.
 
• The ranking is widely regarded as one of the most authoritative reports on the competitiveness of nations, focusing on how nations manage their resources and competencies to increase prosperity.
 
 
 
• **The Four Pillars of Competitiveness:**
 
 
• **Economic Performance:** Evaluates the domestic economy, **International Trade**, **International Investment**, **Employment**, and **Prices**.
 
• **Government Efficiency:** Measures **Public Finance**, **Tax Policy**, **Institutional Framework**, **Business Legislation**, and **Societal Framework**.
 
• **Business Efficiency:** Assesses **Productivity and Efficiency**, **Labor Market**, **Finance**, **Management Practices**, and **Attitudes and Values**.
 
• **Infrastructure:** Looks at **Basic Infrastructure**, **Technological Infrastructure**, **Scientific Infrastructure**, **Health and Environment**, and **Education**.
 
 
 
• **Methodology and Data:**
 
 
• The ranking utilizes a combination of **Hard Data** (representing about **two-thirds** of the weight), which includes statistical indicators from international and national sources, and **Soft Data** (representing **one-third** of the weight) from an **Executive Opinion Survey**.
 
• In **2025**, the criteria were updated to reflect emerging global trends such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption**, **Energy Security**, and **Geopolitical Stability**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for Global Markets:**
 
 
• Economies like **Denmark**, **Ireland**, and **Sweden** often fluctuate within the top ten, highlighting the competitive nature of **European** markets compared to **Asian** powerhouses.
 
• The **2025** rankings specifically highlighted how "small" economies often outperform larger ones like the **USA** or **China** due to their **Agility** and specialized **Economic Policies**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the best description of RHUMI-1, which was seen in the news in August 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India’s first reusable hybrid rocket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RHUMI-1** is **India’s first reusable hybrid rocket**, which represents a major advancement in the nation's private space exploration capabilities.
 
• It was successfully launched on **August 24, 2024**, using a **mobile launcher** positioned at **Thiruvidanthai**, located on the East Coast Road in **Chennai**.
 
• The rocket was developed by **Space Zone India**, a **Chennai**-based space technology startup, in collaboration with the **Martin Group**.
 
• The mission, designated as **Mission RHUMI 2024**, reached a suborbital altitude to deploy its payloads and then successfully initiated its recovery sequence.
 
• It carried a diverse payload consisting of **3 CubeSats** and **50 PICO satellites**, which were designed to study **atmospheric conditions** and **cosmic radiation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hybrid Propulsion System**: **RHUMI-1** utilizes a **hybrid motor** that combines **solid fuel** with a **liquid oxidizer**. This technology is preferred for its **safety** and **cost-effectiveness**, as it is less prone to explosions compared to traditional solid or liquid-only engines and allows for thrust **throttling**.
 
• **Sustainability and Reusability**: The rocket features a **reusable** airframe and an **electrically triggered parachute system** for recovery. This minimizes space debris and significantly reduces the **operational costs** of deploying small satellites into orbit.
 
• **Educational Initiative**: The launch was a centerpiece of the **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Students Space Launch-2024**. This program involved thousands of students from across **India**, providing them with hands-on experience in **satellite fabrication** and **rocket science**.
 
• **Mobile Launch Capability**: Unlike traditional rockets that require fixed launch pads like those at **Sriharikota**, **RHUMI-1** was launched from a **mobile platform**. This demonstrates **flexibility** and the ability to conduct launches from diverse geographical locations with minimal infrastructure.
 
• **NewSpace India**: The success of **RHUMI-1** underscores the growing role of the **private sector** in **India's space ecosystem**, following the government's **2020 space sector reforms** that opened up the industry to non-government entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Payload Specifications**: The **50 PICO satellites** deployed are ultra-small satellites, often weighing between **0.1 kg and 1 kg**. These were programmed to monitor **environmental factors** like **accelerometer** data, **altitude**, and **UV radiation**.
 
• **Leadership**: The development was led by **Anand Megalingam**, the founder of **Space Zone India**, who aimed to make **space technology** more accessible and affordable for research and academic purposes.
 
• **Environmental Impact**: Because the hybrid motor uses non-toxic components and is **reusable**, it is considered much more **eco-friendly** than conventional expendable rockets that leave debris and chemical residues.

questions.question: What is India's score in the SDG Index according to the 10th Sustainable Development Report, 2025?

__ 
 
• The **10th Sustainable Development Report** (SDR), released in **2025**, provides an updated assessment of the progress made by all **United Nations** member states toward the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• According to the report, **India** achieved an overall score of **67** out of **100**. This score indicates India's percentage of total progress toward achieving the **17 SDGs**.
 
• The report is published annually by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. The **2025** edition marks a decade since the world adopted the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development** in **September 2015**.
 
• India’s score of **67** reflects steady progress in certain areas, such as **Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** and **Goal 13 (Climate Action)**, although it also highlights sectors that require urgent attention to meet the **2030** deadline.
 
• The **SDG Index** score is a composite measure that aggregates data across all **17 goals**, providing a clear picture of where a country stands in its development journey compared to the ideal target of **100**.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** 
 
 
• The **SDGs**, also known as the **Global Goals**, were adopted by all **193 UN Member States** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that all people enjoy peace and prosperity by **2030**.
 
• There are **17 Goals** and **169 Targets** that are integrated and indivisible, balancing the three dimensions of sustainable development: the **economic**, **social**, and **environmental**.
 
 
 
• **SDSN and the Report:** 
 
 
• The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** has been operating under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** since **2012**.
 
• The report is led by **Professor Jeffrey Sachs** and uses a rigorous methodology to rank countries based on their distance from the **SDG** targets.
 
 
 
• **India's Internal Monitoring:** 
 
 
• In **India**, the **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency responsible for monitoring the **SDGs**. It released the first **SDG India Index** in **2018** to foster competition among states.
 
• States like **Kerala**, **Tamil Nadu**, and **Himachal Pradesh** have consistently emerged as top performers in the domestic **SDG** rankings.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in 2025:** 
 
 
• The **2025 report** emphasizes that the "SDG stimulus" is crucial, as many developing nations face a massive financing gap. High-income countries like **Finland**, **Sweden**, and **Denmark** usually top the global index with scores exceeding **80**.
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Challenges for India:** While India has made strides in **Goal 1 (No Poverty)** and **Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy)**, the **2025** data suggests significant challenges remain in **Goal 2 (Zero Hunger)**, **Goal 5 (Gender Equality)**, and **Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation)**.
 
• **The 5 Ps:** The **2030 Agenda** is structured around five critical dimensions: **People**, **Planet**, **Prosperity**, **Peace**, and **Partnership**.
 
• **Data Fact:** India's score of **67** is an improvement from previous years, showing a positive trajectory despite global shocks like the **COVID-19 pandemic** and climate-related disasters that affected the **South Asian** region.

questions.question: What was the unemployment rate among youth aged 15-29 in rural areas in May 2025, as per the PLFS?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.7%**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** is a critical survey conducted by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** to estimate key employment and unemployment indicators.
 
• As per the data released for **May 2025**, the **unemployment rate** for the **youth** population, specifically those in the **age group of 15-29 years**, was a focal point of the report.
 
• In **rural areas**, the **unemployment rate** for this specific youth demographic was recorded at **13.7%**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 13.7%.***
 
• The **Unemployment Rate (UR)** is defined as the percentage of persons unemployed among the persons in the **labour force** (which includes both employed persons and those seeking work).
 
• The **PLFS** serves as a primary source of **data** for the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** to monitor the health of the **Indian economy** and the effectiveness of employment schemes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**
 
 
• Launched in **April 2017**, the **PLFS** was established to provide more frequent and reliable **labour force data**.
 
• It has two main objectives: to estimate employment indicators in **Current Weekly Status (CWS)** every three months for **urban areas** and to estimate indicators in both **Usual Status** and **CWS** annually for both **rural** and **urban areas**.
 
 
 
• **Key Definitions:**
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):** The percentage of the population that is either working or seeking work.
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR):** The percentage of employed persons in the total population.
 
• **Unemployment Rate (UR):** The percentage of those in the **labour force** who are currently without work but available for and seeking it.
 
 
 
• **Youth Demographics:**
 
 
• In the context of Indian **government surveys** and the **National Youth Policy**, **youth** is generally defined as persons in the **age group of 15-29 years**.
 
• Monitoring this specific group is essential for addressing **skill development** needs and reducing **demographic** pressures on the **job market**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Measurement Status:**
 
 
• **Usual Status (ps+ss):** This determines the employment status of a person based on a reference period of **365 days** preceding the date of the survey.
 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS):** This determines the status based on a reference period of **7 days** preceding the survey date. A person is considered employed if they worked for at least **one hour** on any day during the reference week.
 
 
 
• **Organizational Framework:**
 
 
• The **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** of the **Government of India**.
 
• Data collected through these surveys influences major policy decisions related to **MGNREGA**, **Skill India**, and other **social security** initiatives.
 
 
</ul
